note: On the commercial criteria this is the strongest fit in the batch and close to the archetype the ICP quote describes. 'successful' is met squarely — a lawyer at a hyper-growth tech startup, senior enough to be hiring into his own team, which is the 'physician or equivalent' bracket. 'income' is met by conduct rather than statement: he raised no affordability objection at any point, asked the fee structure neutrally and responded to £4,500 with 'Oh. That makes sense.' 'neglected_health' is met almost verbatim against the stated criterion — 'my work's quite busy and the expectations are enormous. And that means I always put off just fitness in general.' 'not_deconditioned' holds against the exclusion as written: he is not 50 lb overweight (targeting a 10 kg drop), is not gym-averse, joined a gym two months ago and plays basketball. The one genuine miss is 'good_to_great' — he is not going from good to great, he is rebuilding from a full year of no training and self-reported inability to lift his former weights, which is nearer the rescue end than the optimisation end. That single criterion is what keeps this at edge rather than core, and it is worth noting that starting point is the only place he falls short while being the most obviously affordable prospect in the batch.
